library(httr2)

cache_file <- "../../data/raw/usaspending_awards.csv"

# Palette: two node modes get two categorical hues; edges use a single-hue
# sequential ramp (light = few contracts, dark = many).
col_agency <- "#2a78d6"   # blue   = government (mode 1)

edge_high  <- "#1f1f1d"

## 1. What this graph shows

A **two-mode (bipartite) network** has two kinds of nodes, and edges only run
*between* the kinds, never within them:

* **Mode 1: government**: the federal *awarding sub-agency* (e.g., ICE, FBI, Army).
* **Mode 2: companies**: private data, analytics, and information providers.
* **Edge**: at least one contract from that agency to that company in the period.

Each edge carries **two weights**, and the graph shows both:

| Weight | Encoded as | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Contract size** (total $ obligated) | **edge width** (log scale) | Dollar values span ~6 orders of magnitude; a linear width would make everything but the top edge invisible. |
| **Number of contracts** | **edge color** (light → dark) | Separates *one big contract* (thick, pale) from *many small, recurring ones* (thin, dark), which is a different kind of dependence. |

Node size = the node's total contract dollars (its weighted degree, or "strength").

## 2. Pull the data

The firms below are searched by **recipient name** in the USAspending Award
Search API (contracts only: award types A–D). Edit `firm_queries` to add or
remove companies. Results are cached to `data/raw/usaspending_awards.csv`
so knitting is fast after the first run.

```{r firms}
# search text -> clean firm label (regex used to map messy recipient names)
firm_queries <- tribble(
  ~query,              ~firm,                         ~pattern,
  "LexisNexis",        "RELX / LexisNexis",           "LEXISNEXIS|LEXIS-NEXIS|LEXIS NEXIS",
  "RELX",              "RELX / LexisNexis",           "^RELX|REED ELSEVIER",
  "Thomson Reuters",   "Thomson Reuters (West/CLEAR)","THOMSON REUTERS",
  "West Publishing",   "Thomson Reuters (West/CLEAR)","WEST PUBLISHING",
  "Palantir",          "Palantir",                    "PALANTIR",
  "Babel Street",      "Babel Street",                "BABEL STREET",
  "TransUnion",        "TransUnion",                  "TRANSUNION|TRANS UNION",
  "Equifax",           "Equifax",                     "EQUIFAX",
  "Experian",          "Experian",                    "EXPERIAN",
  "Clearview AI",      "Clearview AI",                "CLEARVIEW AI",
  "Venntel",           "Venntel",                     "VENNTEL",
  "Acxiom",            "Acxiom",                      "ACXIOM",
  "Penlink",           "Penlink",                     "PEN-LINK|PENLINK",
  "ShadowDragon",      "ShadowDragon",                "SHADOWDRAGON|SHADOW DRAGON",
  "Cobwebs",           "Cobwebs",                     "COBWEBS"
)
```

```{r fetch}
fetch_recipient <- function(query, start, end) {
  out <- list(); page <- 1
  repeat {
    body <- list(
      filters = list(
        recipient_search_text = list(query),
        award_type_codes = list("A", "B", "C", "D"),
        time_period = list(list(start_date = start, end_date = end))
      ),
      fields = list("Award ID", "Recipient Name", "Awarding Agency",
                    "Awarding Sub Agency", "Award Amount", "Start Date",
                    "Description"),
      limit = 100, page = page, sort = "Award Amount", order = "desc"
    )
    resp <- request("https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_award/") |>
      req_body_json(body, auto_unbox = TRUE) |>
      req_retry(max_tries = 4) |>
      req_perform() |>
      resp_body_json(simplifyVector = TRUE)
    if (length(resp$results) == 0) break
    out[[page]] <- as_tibble(resp$results)
    if (!isTRUE(resp$page_metadata$hasNext)) break
    page <- page + 1
    Sys.sleep(0.2)   # be polite to the API
  }
  bind_rows(out) |> mutate(query = query)
}

if (params$refresh || !file.exists(cache_file)) {
  raw <- lapply(firm_queries$query, fetch_recipient,
                start = params$start_date, end = params$end_date) |>
    bind_rows()
  write.csv(raw, cache_file, row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  raw <- read.csv(cache_file, check.names = FALSE) |> as_tibble()
}
nrow(raw)
```

## 3. Clean and build the edge list

Different searches can return the same award, and a search can pick up
unrelated companies (e.g., "Clearview" matches more than Clearview AI), so each
recipient name is matched against the firm's regex, and awards are de-duplicated.

```{r clean}
awards <- raw |>
  distinct(`Award ID`, `Recipient Name`, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(recipient = toupper(`Recipient Name`))

# assign each award to the first firm whose pattern matches its recipient name
awards$firm <- NA_character_
for (i in seq_len(nrow(firm_queries))) {
  hit <- is.na(awards$firm) & grepl(firm_queries$pattern[i], awards$recipient)
  awards$firm[hit] <- firm_queries$firm[i]
}

awards <- awards |>
  filter(!is.na(firm), `Award Amount` > 0) |>
  mutate(agency     = `Awarding Agency`,
         sub_agency = `Awarding Sub Agency`,
         amount     = `Award Amount`,
         start      = as.Date(`Start Date`))

# Which raw recipient names were kept? (check for false matches here)
awards |> count(firm, recipient, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r edges}
# keep the top N sub-agencies by spending so the graph stays legible
top_subs <- awards |>
  group_by(sub_agency) |>
  summarise(total = sum(amount)) |>
  slice_max(total, n = params$top_agencies) |>
  pull(sub_agency)

edges <- awards |>
  filter(sub_agency %in% top_subs) |>
  group_by(from = sub_agency, to = firm) |>
  summarise(n_contracts = n(),
            total_amount = sum(amount),
            parent_agency = first(agency),
            .groups = "drop")

nodes <- bind_rows(
  edges |> group_by(name = from) |>
    summarise(strength = sum(total_amount), parent = first(parent_agency)) |>
    mutate(type = "Government agency"),
  edges |> group_by(name = to) |>
    summarise(strength = sum(total_amount)) |>
    mutate(type = "Company", parent = name)
)

g <- tbl_graph(nodes = nodes, edges = edges, directed = FALSE)
cat(sum(nodes$type == "Government agency"), "agencies,",
    sum(nodes$type == "Company"), "companies,",
    nrow(edges), "edges,",
    dollar(sum(edges$total_amount), scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M"), "total\n")
```

```{r scales}
# shared encodings so every plot reads the same way
fmt_dollars <- label_dollar(scale_cut = cut_short_scale())

edge_scales <- list(
  scale_edge_width_continuous(
    name = "Contract size\n(total $, log scale)",
    range = c(0.15, 2.8), trans = "log10", labels = fmt_dollars),
  scale_edge_colour_gradient(
    name = "Number of\ncontracts",
    low = edge_low, high = edge_high, trans = "log10",
    breaks = c(1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300))
)
node_scales <- list(
  scale_fill_manual(name = NULL,
                    values = c("Government agency" = col_agency, "Company" = col_firm)),
  scale_shape_manual(name = NULL,
                     values = c("Government agency" = 22, "Company" = 21)),
  scale_size_area(name = "Node total $", max_size = 10, labels = fmt_dollars,
                  breaks = c(1e8, 5e8, 2e9))
)
node_guides <- guides(
  fill  = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 5)),
  shape = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 5)),
  size  = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = list(shape = 21, fill = "#8a8984", colour = "white")))
net_theme <- theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "#52514e"),
        plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10))
```

## 4. Bipartite layout: government on the left, companies on the right

This is the most literal picture of a two-mode graph. Agencies are grouped by
parent department; companies are placed at the average height of the agencies
they contract with, which keeps crossings down.

```{r bipartite, fig.height = 10}
# y positions: agencies sorted by department then spending
agency_order <- nodes |>
  filter(type == "Government agency") |>
  arrange(parent, desc(strength)) |>
  mutate(y = rev(seq_len(n())))

# companies: weighted barycenter of their agencies' heights
firm_y <- edges |>
  left_join(agency_order |> select(from = name, y), by = "from") |>
  group_by(name = to) |>
  summarise(bary = weighted.mean(y, total_amount)) |>
  arrange(bary) |>
  mutate(y = seq(min(agency_order$y), max(agency_order$y), length.out = n()))

lay <- nodes |>
  left_join(bind_rows(agency_order |> select(name, y),
                      firm_y |> select(name, y)), by = "name") |>
  mutate(x = ifelse(type == "Government agency", 0, 1))

ggraph(g, layout = "manual", x = lay$x, y = lay$y) +
  geom_edge_diagonal(aes(edge_width = total_amount, edge_colour = n_contracts),
                     alpha = 0.55, lineend = "round") +
  geom_node_point(aes(fill = type, shape = type, size = strength),
                  colour = "white", stroke = 0.8) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name,
                     hjust = ifelse(type == "Company", 0, 1),
                     x = x + ifelse(type == "Company", 0.03, -0.03)),
                 size = 3, colour = "#0b0b0b") +
  edge_scales + node_scales +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(add = c(0.9, 0.6))) +
  node_guides +
  labs(title = "Who buys from whom: federal agencies × data providers",
       subtitle = sprintf("Contract awards %s to %s. Width = total $; darkness = number of contracts.",
                          params$start_date, params$end_date)) +
  net_theme
```

## 5. Force-directed layout: clusters and brokers

The same graph laid out by network structure. Companies that sit between many
agencies (high-degree "hubs") pull to the center; agencies that rely on a single
provider sit on the edge.

```{r force, fig.height = 9}
set.seed(431)
ggraph(g, layout = "stress", weights = 1 / log10(total_amount)) +
  geom_edge_link(aes(edge_width = total_amount, edge_colour = n_contracts),
                 alpha = 0.6, lineend = "round") +
  geom_node_point(aes(fill = type, shape = type, size = strength),
                  colour = "white", stroke = 0.8) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name,
                     fontface = ifelse(type == "Company", "bold", "plain")),
                 repel = TRUE, size = 2.9, colour = "#0b0b0b",
                 max.overlaps = 30, bg.colour = "white", bg.r = 0.1) +
  edge_scales + node_scales +
  node_guides +
  labs(title = "Network structure of agency–provider contracting",
       subtitle = "Stress layout. Heavier (more $) ties pull nodes closer together.") +
  net_theme
```

## 6. The same graph as a matrix (read exact values)

A two-mode network *is* a matrix, agencies × companies. This view shows
both weights precisely: **fill = contract dollars**, **number in cell = number of
contracts**. Use it alongside the graph in the paper when readers need exact values.

```{r matrix, fig.height = 9, fig.width = 10}
mat <- edges |>
  mutate(from = factor(from, levels = agency_order$name),
         to   = factor(to, levels = nodes |> filter(type == "Company") |>
                          arrange(desc(strength)) |> pull(name)))

ggplot(mat, aes(x = to, y = from)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = total_amount), colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n_contracts,
                colour = total_amount > 10^mean(log10(range(total_amount)))),
            size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_gradient(name = "Contract size\n(total $, log)",
                      low = "#dbe8f8", high = "#0d3d78",
                      trans = "log10", labels = fmt_dollars) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "#0b0b0b")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = "Agency × provider matrix",
       subtitle = "Cell shade = total contract $; number = count of contracts. Blank = no tie.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "#52514e"))
```

## 7. Before, during, and after a crisis

Your research question is about change across a crisis, so here is the network
split into three windows around COVID-19. Edit `periods` to use other crises
(e.g., FEMA declaration windows). Node positions are fixed across panels so you
can compare which ties appear, thicken, or disappear.

```{r periods, fig.height = 7, fig.width = 14}
periods <- tribble(
  ~period,                 ~from_date,   ~to_date,
  "1. Pre-COVID 2017–19",  "2017-01-01", "2019-12-31",
  "2. COVID 2020–21",      "2020-01-01", "2021-12-31",
  "3. Post-COVID 2022–24", "2022-01-01", "2024-12-31"
) |> mutate(across(c(from_date, to_date), as.Date))

edges_p <- awards |>
  filter(sub_agency %in% top_subs) |>
  cross_join(periods) |>
  filter(start >= from_date, start <= to_date) |>
  group_by(period, from = sub_agency, to = firm) |>
  summarise(n_contracts = n(), total_amount = sum(amount), .groups = "drop")

# one graph holding every period's edges; facet_edges splits them
g_p <- tbl_graph(nodes = nodes, edges = edges_p, directed = FALSE)

ggraph(g_p, layout = "manual", x = lay$x, y = lay$y) +
  geom_edge_diagonal(aes(edge_width = total_amount, edge_colour = n_contracts),
                     alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_node_point(aes(fill = type, shape = type), size = 2.5, colour = "white") +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = ifelse(type == "Company", name, "")),
                 hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.04, size = 2.6) +
  facet_edges(~period) +
  edge_scales + node_scales[1:2] +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(add = c(0.1, 0.9))) +
  labs(title = "How the agency–provider network changes across a crisis",
       subtitle = "Left column = agencies (same order as section 4); right = companies.") +
  net_theme + theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))
```

```{r period-summary}
edges_p |>
  group_by(period) |>
  summarise(ties = n(),
            contracts = sum(n_contracts),
            total = dollar(sum(total_amount), scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M"),
            agencies = n_distinct(from),
            firms = n_distinct(to))
```

## 8. Network statistics

```{r stats}
ig <- as.igraph(g)
V(ig)$type <- V(ig)$type == "Company"   # igraph's bipartite flag

node_stats <- tibble(
  name = V(ig)$name,
  mode = ifelse(V(ig)$type, "Company", "Agency"),
  degree = degree(ig),
  total_dollars = strength(ig, weights = E(ig)$total_amount),
  total_contracts = strength(ig, weights = E(ig)$n_contracts)
) |>
  arrange(mode, desc(total_dollars)) |>
  mutate(total_dollars = dollar(total_dollars, scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M", accuracy = 0.1))

node_stats

# one-mode projection: companies linked when they share an agency client
proj <- bipartite_projection(ig, which = "true")
cat("Company–company density (shared agency clients):",
    round(edge_density(proj), 2), "\n")
```

```{r top-edges}
edges |>
  arrange(desc(total_amount)) |>
  mutate(total_amount = dollar(total_amount)) |>
  select(agency = from, company = to, n_contracts, total_amount) |>
  head(20)
```

## 9. Caveats to note in the paper

* **Data purchases vs. other services.** RELX (which also owns Elsevier) and
  Thomson Reuters (Westlaw) contracts include legal research and journal
  subscriptions as well as person-search products (Accurint, CLEAR). Use the
  `Description` field, or product/service codes, to separate them, as your
  proposal anticipates.
* **Recipient search is name-based.** Check the recipient table in section 3
  for false matches before interpreting a tie.
* **Award Amount** is the total obligated over the award's life, dated by the
  award's start date; multi-year contracts are assigned to the year they began.
* **Sub-agency cut-off.** Only the top `r params$top_agencies` sub-agencies by
  spending are drawn; change `top_agencies` in the YAML header.
